correctness.rationale: Every pointwise kernel is a probability measure, so the total-variation identity gives twice missing fiber mass, including off-fiber atoms. For mixed components, triangle inequality reduces unrestricted error to 2/3 times the connected double-cover m-r term problem; the latter has sharp distance 2/(m-r) by the inspected source Theorem 1.1. The one-component cases are bounded separately and the one-map endpoint handled. Equal-weight lower bounds follow from a nonsection map, hence at least one absent target atom and balanced integral occupancy counts. The explicit residue-class allocation and published labelled-atom transport lemma give continuous maps with defects matching every lower bound for all m, with no finite-enumeration extrapolation. Exact diagnostics report THREE_SHEET_RATIONAL_CHECK_OK 2513 and cover only finite arithmetic and finite labelled swaps.

The identified earlier disconnected-covering formulas are budget two and budget three, respectively. They do not cover the complete split 1+2 covering beyond these budgets. The proof uses a reduction to the connected degree-two factor for arbitrary weights plus a three-position nonsection counting argument for equal weights.

value.rationale: This is the smallest nontrivial partially reducible covering (monodromy one fixed point plus transposed pair). It has an explicit global section but still cannot be finitely represented as a convex sum of extreme Markov maps. The theorem fully classifies all fixed finite budgets, proves attainment, separates free from equal coefficients by sharp limits 3/2 and 2, and unexpectedly preserves the connected degree-three equal-weight errors. Such component-sensitive finite-budget exactness is a natural structural gap singled out by the primary article Remark 6.7, not an arbitrary numerical example. General disconnected coverings and variable fiber weights are not claimed.
